title: Canonicalized change-log serializer for privilege operations
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Define and implement a compact, canonical serializer for audit change-logs emitted by privilege and admin flows (RBAC v2). The serializer must produce a guarded, indexable, query-friendly representation that supports privacy redaction hints, compact diffs, cryptographic change signatures, and efficient storage/retention policies for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v1 defined and approved in this ticket's description
Serializer implemented in audit-producer (Go) and passes unit tests for roundtrip and redaction
Compact diff encoding reduces payload size by >=40% vs naive before/after JSON for typical admin changes
Change-signature (SHA256) present and verifiable for all changed events
Docs and migration guide published: confluence link and GH PR linked
Rollout plan verified with canary on internal org and observed for 72 hours without missing queries
design_decisions: Adopt a typed event envelope: {meta, actor, target, change, op, trace, tags}
Store 'change' as an ordered list of compact tuples (path, op, value_or_delta) to enable efficient diffing and small payloads
Use explicit redaction hints per field (keep|redact|hash) to allow downstream redaction without schema churn
Include a canonical SHA256 change-signature computed over canonicalized tuple sequence to detect tampering and enable compact rollback checks
Index keys: event_id, actor.id, target.id, op.type, resource.type, timestamp, tags.environment
Retention tags (fast-path vs long-term) embedded as event.tags.retention_level: e.g., 'compliance:7y' or 'ephemeral:30d'
Backward compatibility: producer emits legacy 'before'/'after' as optional full payload only when DEBUG mode enabled; consumers must support both v0 and v1 during migration
event_schema: change: list of tuples [path, op, value] encoded as JSON arrays (see diff_format)
tags: list of strings key:value (e.g., environment:prod, retention:7y)
signature: string (hex of SHA256 over canonical change sequence)
redaction_hints: list of strings path:hint (hint in {keep,redact,hash})
diff_format: Compact tuple list. Each change entry is a 3-tuple [path, op, payload] where path is a JSON Pointer-style string, op is one of {set, unset, insert, remove, replace, patch}, and payload is either the value (for set/insert/replace) or a compact delta (for patch). For array edits we use index-based ops. All tuples are sorted deterministically by path to produce canonical signing. Example: [["/roles/0/permissions/3","remove","read:secrets"],["/roles/1/description","replace","Updated role for billing team"]]. The serializer MUST canonicalize keys (utf8 NFC), sort object keys, and normalize timestamps before signing.
retention_and_storage: Events routed to S3-backed coldstore with partitioning by year/month/day and event.meta.id for fast retrieval
Hot store in ClickHouse for 90 days for analytics with TTL policies that migrate to coldstore
Retention tag enforcement through async compactor that applies field-level redaction and deletion based on tags
Compressed with Zstd and stored with small-file aggregation to avoid S3 request explosion
Search index keeps only indexed fields and change-signature; full change payloads retrievable from coldstore only when needed
rollout_plan: 1) Implement serializer library behind feature flag in audit-producer (canary=false)
2) Unit/integration tests and performance benchmark (target <1ms extra per event, compression gain >=40%)
3) Enable canary for internal orgs (redwood-infra) for 24h, monitor queryability and downstream consumers
4) Gradual enable per-org using feature flag targeting: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over two weeks
5) Run data migration job to backfill signatures for last 90 days where possible and surface mismatches
6) Deprecate legacy before/after full payload in 3 months after migration completes
open_questions: Should change-signature be key-signed by a per-cluster KMS key to enable non-repudiation? (ops/security tradeoff)
How to handle large blob properties (policy documents >100KB) — inline with delta or store pointer to blob store?
Do we allow consumers to request 'unredacted' payloads if authorized and audited? Workflow for approval?
Edge case: simultaneous parallel updates to same resource — how do we guarantee deterministic tuple order? Use causal ordering via op.sequence?
